test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 14 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: At what rate of interest per annum will a sum of ₹8,000 amount to ₹15,625 in 1 year and 6 months, if the interest is compounded half-yearly?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Amount (A)** to **Principal (P)** for 3 half-years: A : P = 15625 : 8000 = 125 : 64.

Since the time is **1.5 years (3 half-years)**, take the **cube root** of the ratio parts.

Ratio for 1 half-year period = √³125 : √³64 = 5 : 4.

**Half-yearly Rate** = (5 − 4)/4 × 100 = 1/4 × 100 = 25%.

**Annual Rate (R)** = 25% × 2 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Principal (P)** = ₹8,000, **Amount (A)** = ₹15,625, **Time (t)** = 1 year 6 months = 1.5 years.

**Formula Used:** A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where n = number of periods and r = rate per period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a85d2eeb2f24394a5cf24dc6d40490308d162d278031404ef68f6192900b5c96.png] 

For **half-yearly compounding**, n = 1.5 × 2 = 3 periods.

Let the **half-yearly rate** be r%.

⇒ 15625 = 8000(1 + r/100)³

⇒ 15625/8000 = (1 + r/100)³

⇒ 125/64 = (1 + r/100)³

⇒ (5/4)³ = (1 + r/100)³

⇒ 1 + r/100 = 5/4

⇒ r/100 = 5/4 − 1 = 1/4

⇒ r = 25% (half-yearly rate)

⇒ **Annual Rate (R)** = 2 × r = 2 × 25% = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compounding Frequency

If interest is compounded **half-yearly**, rate becomes **R/2** and time becomes **2T**. If **quarterly**, rate becomes **R/4** and time becomes **4T**.

Effective Annual Rate

It is the actual annual interest rate when compounding occurs more than once a year: **Rₑff = [(1 + r/100)ⁿ − 1] × 100**.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, CI − SI = **P(R/100)²**. For 3 years, CI − SI = **P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100)**.

2d
